newsitem.title: USA: Gillette says dlr strength cut sales growth.
newsitem.headline: Gillette says dlr strength cut sales growth.

text.p: The strength of the U.S. dollar cut three percentage points off Gillette Co sales growth in the second quarter of 1997, although the company managed to post record second quarter and half year net income and income per share.

Gillette said in a statement with earnings that sales rose just one percent in the second quarter from a year ago to $2.29 billion and that net income share per rose 14 percent to 57 cents, on a 15 percent rise in net income to $319 million.
Profit from operations was $517 million, up 10 percent.

"These results are particularly notable given the quarter's constrained sales growth, which reflected the negative impact of foreign currencies, as well as the company's continued assimilation of Duracell's international operations and measures taken in advance of the launch of a new shaving system," said Alfred M. Zeien, chairman and chief executive officer.
For the six months to end-June, sales rose three percent to $4.47 billion, while profit from operations rose 11 percent to $983 million.
Net income was up 15 percent at $603 million and rose 14 percent to $1.08.

Among individual product lines, blade and razor sales were unchanged year on year in both the quarter and the half-year, while profits at the division were up, while Duracell sales rose slightly and the company said profits were up significantly.
For the Braun product line, sales and profits were moderately lower than a year ago.
